reason: Hypothesis B directly addresses the brittle continuous ordered phase limitation in HfZrTiTa0.53 by proposing a phase-inversion heat treatment, which is physically sound for refractory high-entropy alloys and supported by prior evidence (E2) showing ductility improvement via similar microstructural engineering. It is specific, testable, and extends earlier work, whereas Hypothesis A relies on a surface treatment (SMAT) that is unlikely to resolve bulk tensile ductility issues and lacks direct support for this alloy system.
